ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Omnislice.cs:19-22) == cost 0 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY. Note the TARGET type is AnyEnemy even though the card splashes -- the splash is a follow-up, not a fan-out -- and the sim carries ANY_ENEMY, which is what keeps the framework from routing it per-enemy.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(8m, ValueProp.Move)` (Omnislice.cs:17) == `_damage = 8`, powered on both sides for the FIRST hit.

OnPlay.issue: The structure is faithful: powered 8 to the target, then the splash to every OTHER hittable enemy as `Unpowered | Move` (Omnislice.cs:28-40) == `props=DamageProps.CARD_UNPOWERED` (colorless_attacks.py:322-324), and the target set matches -- C#'s `GetTeammatesOf(receiver).Except(target).Where(e => e.IsHittable)` == `[e for e in ctx.enemies if e is not target and not e.is_gone]`. The splash being UNPOWERED is the load-bearing detail and the sim has it right. THE SPLASH AMOUNT IS THE WRONG QUANTITY: C# splashes `damageResult.TotalDamage + damageResult.OverkillDamage` (Omnislice.cs:39). The sim uses `DamageCmd.deal`'s return value, which is `hp_lost` (cmds.py:126) -- HP actually removed -- where C# uses `DamageResult.TotalDamage + OverkillDamage`, and those are precisely `BlockedDamage + UnblockedDamage` (DamageResult.cs:64) plus the excess beyond the target's HP, with `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp` and `OverkillDamage = num - currentHp` on a kill (Creature.LoseHpInternal, Creature.cs:445-457). So C#'s figure is the ENTIRE post-modifier damage the attack put out, and the sim's is only the middle term: it under-reports by the blocked portion and by the overkill. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/fisticuffs's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE, because enemy block is routine and overkill is the normal case late in a fight. Concretely: Omnislice into a target holding 8 block splashes 8 in the game and 0 in the sim; into a 3-HP target it splashes 8 in the game and 3 in the sim. Presentation, folded in: the AttackContext wrapper (Omnislice.cs:27, 29, 38-40), which exists to group the two damage instances into one visual attack.

guards.what: the sim returns early when nothing got through (`if dealt <= 0: return`, colorless_attacks.py:319-320); C# proceeds whenever the DamageResult is non-null (Omnislice.cs:30-31)
guards.rationale: C# would splash a value of 0, which damages nothing. The observable difference is only whether the splash's `BeforeDamageReceived` / `AfterDamageReceived` hooks fire with a 0 amount on the other enemies; the sim's own `DamageCmd.deal` would also run its pipeline for a 0 amount, so the divergence is the sim skipping it. Dormant: no ported listener acts on a zero-damage instance. Note this guard becomes moot once the OnPlay amount is fixed, because C#'s figure is only 0 when the attack was fully blocked AND dealt no overkill.
